activations.domainDescription: Medial prefrontal cortex — self-referential processing, mentalizing, and social cognition in the developing brain
activations.domainFunction: Integrates self-referential thought with social understanding; critical hub for theory of mind development and emotion regulation maturation
activations.whyThisNode: Central to developing theory of mind — mPFC mediates the child's emerging ability to understand their own and others' mental states

treatments.label: Social skills training with mentalizing focus
treatments.description: Structured peer interaction programs (e.g., PEERS) that build perspective-taking and social cognition

treatments.label: Developmental screening for social cognition delays
treatments.description: Administer M-CHAT-R/F at 18 and 24 months; ADOS-2 if screening positive

activations.domainDescription: Basolateral amygdala — fear conditioning, threat detection, and emotional reactivity in developing circuits
activations.domainFunction: Detects and responds to emotional and threatening stimuli; undergoes prolonged maturation with shifting reactivity profiles across childhood
activations.whyThisNode: Amygdala reactivity is implicated in the largest number of pediatric conditions — hyperreactive in anxiety, PTSD, and behavioral disorders; altered in ASD

treatments.label: Trauma-Focused CBT or exposure-based therapy
treatments.description: Gold-standard graduated exposure protocols to reduce amygdala hyperreactivity through extinction learning

treatments.label: Anxiety screening with SCARED or CBCL Internalizing
treatments.description: Standardized assessment of fear and anxiety severity to guide treatment intensity

activations.domainDescription: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex — working memory, sustained attention, and cognitive control in the maturing brain
activations.domainFunction: Supports working memory, attentional control, and cognitive flexibility; undergoes prolonged cortical maturation through adolescence
activations.whyThisNode: Executive function deficits are transdiagnostic across pediatric conditions — dlPFC maturation delays underlie ADHD, depression, and behavioral dysregulation

treatments.label: Stimulant medication trial with standardized monitoring
treatments.description: Methylphenidate or amphetamine-based medication with Conners-3 or SNAP-IV tracking at 2 and 4 weeks

treatments.label: Neuropsychological testing for executive function
treatments.description: Comprehensive evaluation including BRIEF-2, CPT-3, and D-KEFS to map specific executive deficits

activations.domainDescription: Ventrolateral prefrontal cortex — motor inhibition, frustration tolerance, and regulatory control
activations.domainFunction: Inhibits prepotent motor responses and regulates emotional reactions; critical for impulse control and frustration management
activations.whyThisNode: Right IFG is the core inhibitory control region — its immaturity in childhood directly drives impulsivity, emotional outbursts, and oppositional behavior

treatments.label: Parent Management Training (PMT)
treatments.description: Evidence-based parent training in consistent reinforcement, effective commands, and de-escalation strategies

treatments.label: Behavioral observation and functional analysis
treatments.description: Structured observation across settings to identify antecedents and functions of inhibitory failures

activations.domainDescription: Anterior insula — interoceptive awareness, sensory integration, and embodied emotional processing
activations.domainFunction: Processes internal body signals and integrates sensory information with emotional awareness; altered interoception drives somatic symptoms and sensory aversions
activations.whyThisNode: Interoceptive processing is disrupted across multiple pediatric conditions — from alexithymia in ASD to somatic anxiety symptoms to sensory food aversions in ARFID

treatments.label: Occupational therapy for sensory integration
treatments.description: Ayres Sensory Integration protocol or SOS Approach for systematic sensory desensitization

treatments.label: Sensory profile assessment
treatments.description: Administer Sensory Profile-2 or Sensory Processing Measure to map sensory processing patterns

activations.domainDescription: Striatum — reward-based learning, habit formation, and repetitive behavior patterns
activations.domainFunction: Mediates dopaminergic reward processing, procedural learning, and repetitive motor patterns; dysfunction underlies both stereotypies and reward-seeking impulsivity
activations.whyThisNode: Striatal circuits are central to repetitive behaviors in ASD, reward processing deficits in ADHD, and altered punishment sensitivity in ODD

treatments.label: Behavioral intervention targeting repetitive behaviors
treatments.description: Function-based intervention replacing maladaptive repetitive behaviors with adaptive alternatives

treatments.label: Functional behavioral assessment
treatments.description: Identify whether repetitive behaviors serve sensory, communicative, or anxiety-reducing functions

activations.domainDescription: Dorsal anterior cingulate cortex — performance monitoring, conflict detection, and self-evaluation
activations.domainFunction: Monitors errors, detects cognitive conflict, and drives self-evaluative processes; hyperactivation produces excessive self-criticism while hypoactivation impairs error correction
activations.whyThisNode: dACC dysfunction is a transdiagnostic feature — overactive self-monitoring in depression, underactive error correction in ADHD, and hostile attribution bias in ODD

treatments.label: Cognitive restructuring adapted for developmental level
treatments.description: Age-appropriate CBT techniques targeting negative self-evaluation and hostile attribution biases

treatments.label: Self-monitoring skills assessment
treatments.description: Evaluate error awareness and self-evaluation patterns through structured tasks and clinical observation

activations.domainDescription: Nucleus accumbens — reward anticipation, motivation, and pleasure processing in developing circuits
activations.domainFunction: Processes reward anticipation and hedonic value; hypofunction produces anhedonia while altered signaling drives delay aversion and impulsive reward-seeking
activations.whyThisNode: Reward circuit dysfunction is central to both anhedonia in pediatric depression and delay aversion in ADHD — two of the most common childhood conditions

treatments.label: Behavioral activation with pleasant event scheduling
treatments.description: Systematic re-engagement with rewarding activities; age-appropriate activity scheduling with mastery and pleasure ratings

treatments.label: Anhedonia and motivation assessment
treatments.description: Evaluate reward responsiveness using CDI-2 anhedonia subscale and clinical interview

activations.domainDescription: Hippocampus — contextual memory encoding, fear context discrimination, and stress vulnerability
activations.domainFunction: Encodes contextual memories and discriminates safe from dangerous environments; vulnerable to cortisol-mediated damage during development, leading to fear overgeneralization
activations.whyThisNode: Hippocampal development is uniquely vulnerable in childhood — cortisol exposure from depression, trauma, and chronic anxiety can impair its maturation and produce lasting memory and contextual deficits

treatments.label: Trauma narrative processing within TF-CBT
treatments.description: Guided construction and processing of trauma narrative to consolidate and contextualize fragmented trauma memories

treatments.label: Trauma history screening with UCLA PTSD-RI
treatments.description: Systematic screening for trauma exposure and PTSD symptoms using validated pediatric measures

activations.domainDescription: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis — cortisol regulation, stress reactivity, and developmental programming
activations.domainFunction: Regulates cortisol secretion in response to stress; dysregulation during development can produce lasting changes in stress reactivity and impair hippocampal and prefrontal maturation
activations.whyThisNode: The developing HPA axis is uniquely sensitive to environmental stress — early dysregulation predicts depression recurrence and compounds trauma effects on the developing brain

treatments.label: Structured physical activity program (30-60 min, 3-5x/week)
treatments.description: Regular aerobic exercise normalizes HPA axis function, upregulates BDNF, and has antidepressant-equivalent effects

treatments.label: Cortisol and metabolic screening
treatments.description: Assess morning cortisol, thyroid function, and inflammatory markers in treatment-resistant presentations

crossDomainAffinities.role: Attentional Control — Feedback & Validation — Tertiary Node

activations.domainDescription: Raphe nuclei — serotonergic modulation of mood, anxiety, and impulse control in the maturing brain
activations.domainFunction: Provides serotonergic innervation to cortical and limbic circuits; still developing through adolescence, which explains both SSRI efficacy and activation syndrome risk in youth
activations.whyThisNode: The serotonin system is the primary pharmacological target in pediatric mood and anxiety disorders — its incomplete maturation in childhood requires careful dosing and monitoring

treatments.label: SSRI trial with FDA Black Box monitoring protocol
treatments.description: Fluoxetine (ages 8+) or escitalopram (ages 12+) with weekly face-to-face monitoring for first month per FDA guidelines

treatments.label: Mood and suicidality monitoring during SSRI initiation
treatments.description: PHQ-A and Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale at each visit during SSRI titration

activations.domainDescription: Superior temporal sulcus — processing of biological motion, gaze direction, and social perception
activations.domainFunction: Processes dynamic social signals including eye gaze, facial expressions, body language, and vocal prosody; underactivation impairs social perception
activations.whyThisNode: STS is a core component of the social brain network — its hypoactivation in ASD directly maps to the social perception deficits that define the condition

treatments.label: Social skills groups with video modeling
treatments.description: Structured peer interaction practice using video feedback to train social perception of gaze, gesture, and prosody

treatments.label: Social communication assessment
treatments.description: Administer SRS-2 and pragmatic language evaluation to quantify social perception deficits

activations.domainDescription: Fusiform gyrus — face recognition, visual word form processing, and category-specific identification
activations.domainFunction: Specialized for face processing (right) and visual word recognition (left); dual role in ASD face processing deficits and dyslexia reading deficits
activations.whyThisNode: The fusiform serves double duty in pediatric conditions — its right lateralization for faces is hypoactive in ASD, while its left lateralization for words fails to develop in dyslexia

treatments.label: Structured literacy intervention targeting visual word form
treatments.description: Orton-Gillingham-based multisensory phonics to develop left fusiform automatized word recognition

treatments.label: Reading fluency and face recognition assessment
treatments.description: WIAT-4 Word Reading and Pseudoword Decoding subtests; clinical observation of face processing

activations.domainDescription: Temporoparietal junction — perspective-taking, mental state attribution, and self-other distinction
activations.domainFunction: Supports mentalizing and perspective-taking by computing others' beliefs, intentions, and mental states; core component of the social brain network
activations.whyThisNode: TPJ hypoactivation during theory of mind tasks is one of the most replicated findings in ASD neuroimaging — it directly maps to the mentalizing deficit

treatments.label: Parent-mediated intervention (ESDM or JASPER)
treatments.description: Naturalistic developmental behavioral interventions training parents as primary interventionists for social engagement

treatments.label: Theory of mind developmental assessment
treatments.description: Evaluate false belief understanding, perspective-taking, and mental state language through structured tasks

activations.domainDescription: Cerebellum — motor coordination, timing, procedural learning, and skill automatization
activations.domainFunction: Coordinates motor output, encodes precise timing, and automates learned skills; cerebellar deficits impair motor development, reading automatization, and attention timing
activations.whyThisNode: Cerebellar abnormalities are found across ASD (Purkinje cell loss), ADHD (volume reduction), and dyslexia (automatization deficit) — a transdiagnostic pediatric finding

treatments.label: Motor skills intervention and coordination training
treatments.description: Occupational or physical therapy targeting motor planning, coordination, and timing deficits

treatments.label: Motor coordination screening (MABC-2)
treatments.description: Movement Assessment Battery for Children to identify developmental coordination disorder comorbidity

activations.domainDescription: Corpus callosum — white matter tract connecting hemispheres; critical for integrated processing
activations.domainFunction: Enables interhemispheric communication and integration; thinning or delayed development disrupts cross-hemisphere coordination of cognitive and motor functions
activations.whyThisNode: Corpus callosum structural abnormalities are consistently found in both ASD and ADHD — reflecting the broader connectivity disruptions that characterize neurodevelopmental conditions

treatments.label: Bimanual coordination and cross-midline activities
treatments.description: Targeted activities requiring interhemispheric coordination to strengthen callosal pathways

treatments.label: Structural neuroimaging if clinically indicated
treatments.description: MRI brain if regression, focal neurological signs, or atypical presentation warrants structural evaluation

activations.domainDescription: Language network — speech production, comprehension, and pragmatic language development
activations.domainFunction: Integrates phonological, semantic, and pragmatic language processing; atypical connectivity in ASD disrupts pragmatic language while structural differences in dyslexia impair phonological processing
activations.whyThisNode: Language network development is central to both ASD (pragmatic language deficits) and dyslexia (phonological processing deficits) — the two most common neurodevelopmental referral reasons

treatments.label: Speech-language therapy targeting specific deficits
treatments.description: Pragmatic language intervention for ASD; phonological awareness training for dyslexia; AAC for minimally verbal children

treatments.label: Comprehensive language evaluation
treatments.description: CELF-5 for receptive/expressive language; CTOPP-2 for phonological processing; pragmatic language assessment

crossDomainAffinities.role: Default Mode / Self-Referential Processing Coordination & Integration

activations.domainDescription: Angular gyrus — phonological decoding, letter-sound correspondence, and cross-modal integration
activations.domainFunction: Converts between phonological and orthographic representations; hypoactivation is the core neural signature of dyslexia
activations.whyThisNode: Angular gyrus hypoactivation during phonological tasks is the most robust neuroimaging finding in developmental dyslexia — it is the neural bottleneck for learning to read

treatments.label: Systematic multisensory phonics instruction
treatments.description: Orton-Gillingham, Wilson, or Barton structured literacy program with explicit phoneme-grapheme mapping

treatments.label: Phonological awareness and rapid naming assessment
treatments.description: CTOPP-2 phonological awareness, phonological memory, and rapid naming composites

activations.domainDescription: Broca's area — speech production, phonological output, and compensatory reading strategies
activations.domainFunction: Generates speech motor programs and supports phonological output; shows compensatory overactivation in dyslexia as effortful decoding replaces automatic recognition
activations.whyThisNode: Left IFG compensatory overactivation in dyslexia reflects the shift from automatic to effortful reading — a hallmark of the dyslexic brain's adaptive strategy

treatments.label: Fluency-building reading intervention
treatments.description: Repeated reading of connected text to build automatized word recognition and reduce compensatory effortful decoding

treatments.label: Oral reading fluency assessment (DIBELS or AIMSweb)
treatments.description: Timed oral reading fluency probes to quantify automaticity deficit and track intervention response

activations.domainDescription: Orbitofrontal cortex — social reward processing, food valuation, and contingency learning
activations.domainFunction: Computes reward value of social and food stimuli; dysfunction impairs social learning in ODD and reduces food reward valuation in ARFID
activations.whyThisNode: OFC links social and appetitive reward systems — its dysfunction in ODD impairs learning from social consequences while in ARFID it reduces the hedonic value of food

treatments.label: Collaborative and Proactive Solutions (CPS)
treatments.description: Identify lagging skills and unsolved problems; collaborative problem-solving to build social contingency learning

treatments.label: Functional behavioral assessment across settings
treatments.description: Map reward and punishment sensitivity patterns through structured observation and caregiver interview

activations.domainDescription: Bed nucleus of the stria terminalis — sustained anticipatory anxiety and threat vigilance
activations.domainFunction: Maintains sustained anxiety states in response to uncertain or future threats; drives the anticipatory worry about separation that characterizes separation anxiety
activations.whyThisNode: BNST extends amygdala-mediated acute fear into sustained anticipatory anxiety — the hallmark of separation anxiety where children dread upcoming separations

treatments.label: Graduated exposure with response prevention
treatments.description: Systematic desensitization to separation situations using fear hierarchy with therapist and parent coaching

treatments.label: Anxiety severity monitoring
treatments.description: Track anticipatory anxiety with daily separation ratings and SCARED subscale scores

crossDomainAffinities.role: Default Mode / Self-Referential Processing Core Operations

activations.domainDescription: Locus coeruleus — noradrenergic arousal, hypervigilance, and startle response modulation
activations.domainFunction: Regulates noradrenergic tone and arousal level; hyperactivation drives the hypervigilance, exaggerated startle, and sleep disruption seen in pediatric PTSD
activations.whyThisNode: LC hyperactivation produces the hyperarousal cluster of PTSD symptoms — hypervigilance, exaggerated startle, and sleep-onset difficulty that are particularly disabling in children

treatments.label: Prazosin for trauma-related nightmares
treatments.description: Alpha-1 antagonist to reduce noradrenergic hyperarousal; effective for trauma nightmares and sleep disruption

treatments.label: Hyperarousal symptom assessment
treatments.description: UCLA PTSD Reaction Index hyperarousal subscale; sleep diary; startle response clinical evaluation

activations.domainDescription: GABA/glutamate system — excitatory-inhibitory balance critical for neural circuit maturation
activations.domainFunction: Maintains the excitation-inhibition ratio that is essential for proper circuit development; imbalance alters sensory processing, seizure threshold, and neural noise
activations.whyThisNode: E/I imbalance is a foundational mechanism in ASD neurobiology — elevated glutamate:GABA ratio alters sensory processing, social cognition, and repetitive behavior circuits

treatments.label: Monitor for seizure comorbidity
treatments.description: EEG if clinical concern for seizures; epilepsy prevalence 20-30% in ASD with intellectual disability

treatments.label: Environmental sensory modification
treatments.description: Reduce environmental sensory load to decrease excitatory input burden in E/I imbalanced circuits

activations.domainDescription: Default mode network — mind-wandering, self-referential thought, and task-negative processing
activations.domainFunction: Normally suppressed during focused tasks; failure to suppress DMN during task engagement is a hallmark of ADHD attentional lapses
activations.whyThisNode: DMN-task network anticorrelation failure is one of the most robust biomarkers of ADHD — the brain's inability to suppress mind-wandering during tasks drives inattention

treatments.label: Mindfulness-based attention training
treatments.description: Age-adapted mindfulness exercises to strengthen DMN suppression during focused attention

treatments.label: Continuous performance test (CPT-3)
treatments.description: Objective measure of sustained attention, variability, and DMN intrusion patterns

activations.domainDescription: Oxytocin system — social bonding, trust, attachment formation, and affiliative behavior
activations.domainFunction: Modulates social bonding, trust, and attachment formation; developmental differences in oxytocin signaling contribute to social engagement deficits
activations.whyThisNode: Oxytocin system differences in ASD contribute to social bonding challenges — and oxytocin-mediated attachment is the foundation upon which all pediatric social development builds

treatments.label: Attachment-based intervention (CPP or Circle of Security)
treatments.description: Strengthen caregiver-child attachment through dyadic therapy focused on reading and responding to social cues

treatments.label: Attachment pattern assessment
treatments.description: Clinical evaluation of attachment security, separation response patterns, and social engagement quality

issues.label: Autism Spectrum Disorder
issues.summary: Atypical connectivity with long-range underconnectivity and local overconnectivity; social brain network hypoactivation; altered pruning and minicolumn organization in developing brain

circuits.detail: Medial prefrontal cortex reduced activation during self-referential and social cognition
DMN coherence reduced in developing brain; weak autobiographical narrative integration
Superior temporal sulcus underactivated during biological motion and social perception tasks
Fusiform face area hypoactivation — reduced face processing; may reflect reduced social attention
Temporoparietal junction hypoactivated during theory of mind tasks — mentalizing deficit
Oxytocin system differences — social bonding challenges; developmental trajectory unclear
Anterior insula altered interoception — contributes to emotional awareness and alexithymia in ASD
Amygdala reactivity to social stimuli variable across development; hyperactive in childhood, may normalize by adolescence
Cerebellar Purkinje cell loss and vermis hypoplasia — motor, timing, and cognitive deficits
Corpus callosum thinning — reduced interhemispheric connectivity; contributes to integration deficits
Repetitive behaviors linked to striatal circuit dysfunction; emerging evidence in pediatric populations
Language network atypical connectivity; delayed or different developmental trajectory
Excitation/inhibition imbalance — elevated glutamate:GABA ratio in developing ASD brain

issues.label: ADHD — Combined Presentation
issues.summary: Combined prefrontal hypofunction affecting both attention and inhibitory control circuits; dual deficit model with executive function and motivational circuit dysfunction; cortical maturation delay of ~3 years

circuits.detail: Dorsolateral PFC hypoactivated for working memory and sustained attention
Right IFG hypoactivated for motor inhibition — combined attention and inhibition deficit
Striatal dopamine dysfunction — reduced DA availability in both dorsal and ventral striatum
Failure to suppress DMN during task — DMN-task network anticorrelation disrupted
Error monitoring and conflict detection impaired
Altered reward processing — delay aversion component contributing to impulsive choices
Cerebellar volume reduced — timing deficits affect both motor and cognitive domains
Corpus callosum development delayed — interhemispheric communication deficit

issues.label: Specific Learning Disorder — Reading (Dyslexia)
issues.summary: Left hemisphere reading network disruption; posterior temporo-parietal underactivation impairs phoneme-grapheme mapping; visual word form area fails to develop automatized recognition

circuits.detail: Angular gyrus hypoactivation — impaired phoneme-grapheme mapping (letter-sound correspondence)
Left fusiform gyrus (visual word form area) fails to develop — no automatic word recognition
Left IFG shows compensatory overactivation during phonological processing (effortful decoding)
Auditory cortex shows reduced sensitivity to rapid temporal auditory cues (phonological deficit)
Arcuate fasciculus integrity reduced — impaired connection between phonological and orthographic systems
Magnocellular visual pathway deficits — rapid visual processing impairment in some dyslexics
Cerebellar automation theory — cerebellar dysfunction impairs skill automatization in reading

issues.label: Major Depressive Disorder — Child-Onset
issues.summary: Immature prefrontal-limbic regulatory capacity with amygdala hyperreactivity to negative stimuli; reward circuit hypofunction producing anhedonia; HPA axis hyperactivation with potential hippocampal developmental impact

circuits.detail: Amygdala hyperreactive to negative faces and stimuli — developing brain has less prefrontal regulation
Rumination-related DMN hyperconnectivity — self-referential negative processing similar to adults
Ventral striatum hypofunction — reward processing deficit produces anhedonia
Prefrontal cortex still maturing — less capacity for cognitive reappraisal and emotion regulation
Cortisol elevation may impair developing hippocampus; HPA dysregulation predicts recurrence
Hippocampal volume reduction in pediatric depression; vulnerability to cortisol neurotoxicity during development
Serotonergic system still developing — basis for SSRI treatment but also explains activation syndrome risk
Error and conflict monitoring overactive — excessive self-criticism and negative self-evaluation

issues.label: Separation Anxiety Disorder
issues.summary: Developmentally inappropriate and excessive anxiety about separation from attachment figures; amygdala-medial PFC circuit dysfunction with hyperactive threat detection specific to separation cues; catastrophic cognitions about harm during separation

circuits.detail: Amygdala hyperreactive to separation cues — threat detection amplified for attachment-related stimuli
Extended amygdala sustains anticipatory anxiety about future separations
Medial PFC fails to downregulate separation fear — impaired safety learning
Interoceptive awareness amplified — somatic symptoms (stomachache, nausea) during anticipated separation
Hippocampal contextual memory encodes separation situations as dangerous — overgeneralized fear
Periaqueductal gray panic circuitry activated during actual or threatened separation

issues.label: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder — Pediatric
issues.summary: Fear conditioning model with amygdala-hippocampal circuit encoding trauma memory inadequately extinguished by mPFC; children may express re-experiencing through repetitive play rather than flashbacks; HPA axis dysregulation compounds developmental effects

circuits.detail: Amygdala hyperreactive to trauma reminders — fear conditioning is strong and persistent
Medial PFC fails to extinguish conditioned fear — trauma memory cannot be inhibited
Hippocampus impaired contextual processing — trauma memory fragments generalize to safe contexts
HPA axis dysregulation — may show elevated or blunted cortisol depending on trauma type and chronicity
Locus coeruleus hyperactive — noradrenergic overdrive causes hypervigilance and exaggerated startle
Dissociative circuitry activated in severe trauma — emotional numbing, depersonalization, derealization

issues.label: Oppositional Defiant Disorder
issues.summary: Pattern of angry/irritable mood and argumentative/defiant behavior; prefrontal-amygdala emotion regulation failure with reward processing abnormalities; irritable subtype predicts later anxiety/depression while headstrong subtype predicts conduct disorder

circuits.detail: Amygdala hyperreactive to perceived provocation and unfairness — drives angry/irritable mood dimension
Ventrolateral PFC fails to regulate emotional responses — poor frustration tolerance
Orbitofrontal cortex dysfunction — impaired processing of social rewards and punishments
Striatal reward processing abnormal — heightened sensitivity to reward, reduced sensitivity to punishment
Conflict detection hyperactive in social situations — interprets ambiguous situations as hostile
Executive function deficits — difficulty with cognitive flexibility and response inhibition

issues.label: Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder
issues.summary: Eating disturbance with persistent failure to meet nutritional needs, NOT driven by body image; three profiles — sensory sensitivity, fear of aversive consequences, and lack of interest in eating; interoceptive and sensory processing abnormalities

circuits.detail: Insula sensory processing hyperactive — tastes, textures, smells experienced as aversive or overwhelming
Somatosensory cortex hyperreactive to oral textures — food textures trigger disgust and avoidance
Amygdala fear conditioning to food-related negative experiences (choking, vomiting) in fear-based profile
Hypothalamic hunger signaling reduced — appetite and hunger cues genuinely diminished in lack-of-interest profile
Orbitofrontal food reward valuation altered — food is not experienced as rewarding or pleasurable
Vagal afferent signaling to brainstem altered — interoceptive disconnect between body needs and eating behavior
